articles.title: Jalen Hurts Had Cold Message for Jeffery Simmons After Eagles Stole Win Over the Titans
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles had heard enough from Jeffery Simmons by the time Sunday afternoon was over. The Tennessee Titans star had spent the week talking abo...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles had heard enough from Jeffery Simmons by the time Sunday afternoon was over. The Tennessee Titans star had spent the week talking about how his defense wanted to handle Jalen Hurts , and Tennessee nearly backed those words up with a late upset.

Philadelphia ultimately escaped Nashville with a 24-20 victory, and Hurts made sure Simmons knew exactly who got the final word.

The moment came while Hurts was beginning his postgame interview with FOX Sports. Simmons walked over to congratulate the Eagles quarterback, and Hurts greeted him with a smile before delivering a pointed response.

"You started that sh**, I had to finish it," Hurts told Simmons after the game.

Heavy will leave out the expletive, but Hurts' message was simple: Simmons started it, and Hurts had to finish it. Hurts also added 'much love' as he and Simmons had a positive exchange.

Jalen Hurts Clearly Remembered Jeffery Simmons' Words

This was not a random postgame exchange between two stars. Simmons had drawn attention before kickoff when he explained that Tennessee needed to limit Hurts' rushing ability and force him to win as a passer. The wording quickly made its way around Philadelphia, even though Simmons later maintained that he was discussing defensive strategy rather than trying to disrespect Hurts.

Hurts apparently heard every bit of it. When asked after the game whether Simmons' comments had reached him, the Eagles quarterback confirmed that they had. He did not need a lengthy response after that because Philadelphia's final possession had already provided one.

Tennessee moved ahead 20-17 with 1:56 remaining, leaving Hurts with one final opportunity. He responded by directing a nine-play, 65-yard drive and connecting with Darius Cooper for a 3-yard touchdown with nine seconds left. Hurts finished with 264 passing yards and two touchdowns despite throwing two interceptions earlier in the afternoon.

Eagles Made Sure Simmons Didn't Get the Last Word

Simmons had plenty of reason to feel confident before that final drive. Tennessee's defense had made life difficult for Hurts, and the Titans were less than two minutes away from handing Philadelphia its first loss of the season. Simmons also played with the type of emotion that has made him one of Tennessee's defensive leaders.

That is what made the postgame exchange land so perfectly for Eagles fans. Simmons did not hide from Hurts after the loss, and the interaction between the two players appeared competitive rather than hostile. Still, Hurts was not going to let the opportunity pass without reminding Simmons how the afternoon ended.

Simmons talked before the game. Tennessee grabbed the lead late. Hurts then drove Philadelphia down the field and ripped the victory away with nine seconds remaining. No speech was necessary after that. Simmons started the conversation. Hurts got to finish it.

articles.title: Falcons WR Drake London regrets getting into verbal altercation with fan amid blowout loss to Panthers
articles.summary: Drake London had to be held back by a teammate in the third quarter while getting into it with a fan.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London had to be held back after getting into a verbal confrontation with a fan during a blowout loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

It's unclear what sparked the incident, but London swore at someone in the stands at Mercedes-Benz Stadium midway through the third quarter of the team's 34-3 loss to the Panthers. Olamide Zaccheaus got between London and the fan, who was not seen on the Fox cameras.

London said after the game that he regretted his actions and that it wasn't the "right thing to do," but that some "personal stuff" was said to him.

"I'm going to be honest here, I don't take light to disrespect at all," London said, via ESPN's Marc Raimondi . "I don't care who you are. I'm a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it's not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations."

The Falcons fell to 0-2 after Sunday's loss, and their offense looked rough throughout the contest. London had a team-high 51 receiving yards on four catches, though quarterback Cooper Rush went just 10-of-17 for 86 yards with two interceptions before he was benched in favor of Jack Strand.

Strand threw a pick 6 on his first pass of the day, so he wasn't any better.

London finished with 4 catches for 51 yards on 5 targets.

The Falcons are still without quarterbacks Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa , who are recovering from ACL and oblique injuries, respectively.

While it's not hard to see why things have been an issue for the Falcons' offense this season, that hasn't made things any easier — and absolutely played into London's reaction when he got into it with the person in the stands.

"But with how the game was going and what was said to me, I don't like it," he said.

London, who the Falcons selected with the No. 8 overall draft pick in 2022, signed a four-year, $141 million extension with the team this past offseason. He had 919 receiving yards and seven touchdowns last season, but was limited to 12 games due to various injuries.

The Falcons will take on the Green Bay Packers next on Thursday, which marks the first of three straight prime-time games. If they can't beat the Packers, it'll mark their worst start since the 2020 campaign when they opened the year on a five-game losing streak.

articles.title: Presley Gerber, Cindy Crawford's son, dies aged 27
articles.summary: His family asked for privacy during a "very difficult and painful time" following the model's death.
articles.body:
Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, has died at the age of 27.

Gerber, a model, died at a rehab facility on Sunday, according to records filed by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. The cause of death was not listed.

Allie Jenkins, a representative for Crawford and her husband Rande Gerber, told the BBC's US news partner CBS: "The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time."

Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his runway debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

He went on to model for brands including Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana, and Bottega Veneta.

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use.

In 2023, he told the Studio 22 podcast: "Having struggled with mental health, depression and some other things that come along with that, I think that whether I help one person or a hundred people get out of that place that I was in at one point in my life, that's all I need to do."

And in this month's American Vogue , Kaia discussed her brother's struggles with addiction. She said: "When something like that happens in a family, it kind of levels everyone.

"I think that's also why I started to self-identify as the easy one and never wanted to ask for help."

She added: "My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn't share anything - and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, 'I'm gonna be very human for everyone.' There's only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you're ashamed of them."

Gerber had previously spoken of his close relationship with his family, including Kaia, who he appeared alongside in a campaign for Calvin Klein in 2018, and whose name he had tattooed on his arm.

He told People Magazine that year: "We're a close family, especially me and my sister, so it's definitely cool.

"We get to travel together half of the time, so it makes it a lot less lonely."

Gerber also starred alongside his mother in Pepsi's 2018 Super Bowl commercial, 26 years after Crawford first appeared in her famous 1992 advertisement for the brand.

"We're a really tight family, so it was just like going to work with one of your friends. It was so fun, and easy," he told People Magazine at the time.

In July, Crawford shared two childhood photographs of her son on Instagram to mark his 27th birthday.

"I'm so proud of the man you've become, but I'll always see you as my little boy! Love you," she wrote.

articles.title: The Chiefs and Patrick Mahomes look like their old selves, but now with new help
articles.summary: With playmakers surrounding Patrick Mahomes, and late-game moxie that helped them survive a wild overtime play, the Kansas City Chiefs improved to 2-0.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs last season lost more than Patrick Mahomes, their franchise cornerstone player, to a season-ending injury. Well before the star quarterback injured two ligaments in his left knee last December, the Chiefs had already lost the air of invincibility they’d built while becoming the NFL’s most-feared team in close games. That quality had earned the Chiefs three Super Bowl titles under coach Andy Reid, and a 17-game winning streak in games decided by 8 points or less. That streak was snapped in last year’s first game, and from there only got worse. By last season’s end, their record in one-score games was 1-9, a turnaround some attributed to Mahomes’ inconsistent play before his injury, or a supporting cast of receivers and running backs had grown thin. Tight end Travis Kelce, one of the most prolific pass-catchers in the position’s history, was in the middle of one of his worst statistical seasons. On the ground, the Chiefs ranked near the league’s bottom third in yards per carry. But two games into this new season, Kansas City is 2-0 and again looks like a team that could be feared in the AFC. Mahomes appears uninhibited by his knee injury, and now has a number of playmakers surrounding him — led by a familiar face, and one new. And in Sunday’s 33-30 overtime win against Indianapolis, the Chiefs showed again they know how to win a close game while overcoming a wild play that might have changed the outcome. “There was never a doubt that we were going to get that win,” Kelce said. A walk-off 40-yard field goal as time expired by Harrison Butker gave the Chiefs their eighth consecutive overtime win in the regular season, tying an NFL record also held by San Francisco (2003-10). Mahomes, who threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, now has 25 career game-winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime. The Chiefs join Las Vegas, Cincinnati and Buffalo as the only remaining undefeated teams in the AFC. “That’s what this NFL is about is just finding a way to win games,” Mahomes said on NBC’s “Sunday Night Football.” Kansas City thought it had the game won with five minutes remaining in overtime. Tied at 30-30, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones connected with Laquon Treadwell for a 48-yard gain down to Kansas City’s 17-yard line when Treadwell bobbled and recovered the catch while evading one tackle by L’Jarius Sneed. Trying to gain more yardage, Treadwell was then tackled by Chiefs cornerback Nohl Williams, who punched the ball out for a fumble recovered by Kansas City. Under regular-season overtime rules that have been in place since 2025 that allow each team at least one possession each, Kansas City believed it had won the game by forcing a turnover and stopping the Colts short of tying the game on its first overtime drive. An official review, however, found that Sneed’s left hand grazed the right hip of Treadwell at the same time he secured his bobbled catch — a brush of a few fingers that was barely enough to count Treadwell as down by contact, however slight, at that moment. It negated the fumble that followed. The Colts were still alive. A touchdown would win the game for Indianapolis, but three plays later it still wasn’t close to the end zone. On fourth and 8, 15 yards from a score, the Colts put their offense on the field and looked ready to snap if they had seen the defense they wanted. When they didn’t, the Colts kicked the field goal for a 30-30 tie. By doing so, Mahomes was left with plenty of time to mount a comeback. “Had a play called,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said of the fourth-down decision. “Had to love the look to run it there.” Mahomes jogged into the huddle with 3:06 remaining in overtime knowing the next score would win. He and the Chiefs made it a reality by turning to the franchise’s newest weapon, Kenneth Walker, the Most Valuable Player of last February’s Super Bowl for Seattle who became the team’s prized offseason signing as a free agent. Walker rushed the ball three times for 18 yards, caught a 22-yard pass from Mahomes, and rushed two more yards to set up Butker’s game-winning kick. One week after producing a career-high 191 yards from scrimmage during his Chiefs debut in Week 1, a total helped by Walker’s league-best 14 broken tackles, he finished with 117 rushing yards on 24 carries and added 61 yards receiving against the Colts. Walker has looked every bit the missing piece capable of taking pressure off of Mahomes on the ground and opening up the passing game. “We able to, I guess, freestyle it,” Walker told NBC in a postgame interview of his connection with Mahomes. “If I’m open or if somebody open, play break down, he able to make plays, so it’s great to play with him.” Even more encouraging for Kansas City was not just how quickly a new addition in Walker has integrated into the offense, but how much Kelce — the record-breaking tight end who helped jump-start the team’s dynasty alongside Mahomes — resembled his old self Sunday. Kelce has debated whether to retire each of the last two offseasons after producing career-low yardage totals and just eight touchdowns combined in 2024-25. He was targeted on fewer than seven passes per game last season. On Sunday, a faster, more agile Kelce was targeted 11 times, more than any Chiefs pass-catcher. He caught nine passes for 101 yards including a touchdown that left his pop superstar wife, Taylor Swift, pointing to her wedding ring in a suite in celebration. It was his first game with 100-plus yards and a touchdown since Week 7 of 2023. Kelce now has 128 yards after contact this season, the most in his career through a season’s first two games, per ESPN. “We’re in a zone right now where everybody’s feeding off each other and it’s only making us better and it’s making us play harder for each other.” The contributions from Mahomes and his co-stars, and the team’s late-game moxie, have kept the Chiefs undefeated. Still to be seen is whether those factors also can reverse a troubling trend over the course of a long season. Between 2017-22, the Chiefs ranked among the league’s 10 best in scoring every season and led the NFL in points in 2018 and 2022. In the last three years, though, they ranked 15th in both 2023 and 2024 before dropping to 21st last season. “The parity in this league is crazy,” Chiefs coach Reid said. “You’re going to have some once-score games. You have to bear down, and our guys did that.”

articles.title: NFL Week 2 Sunday takeaways: Packers are Jekyll and Hyde, Bengals have a defense, Chargers' season is over
articles.summary: From the Packers' comeback win over the Jets to Caleb Williams' injury scare, every NFL Week 2 Sunday game delivered surprising takeaways.
articles.body: One week of NFL football gives fans and the media something to talk about. Two weeks gives them just enough information to start believing that they might actually know something (they still don't, and that includes me). Week 2 offered the first chance to see which opening-week performances were meaningful and which were complete mirages. Although, thanks to confirmation bias, nothing that happened probably changed anyone's opinion (including mine). Below, you will find my biggest takeaway from each game on the Week 2 Sunday slate. Panthers 34, Falcons 3 Takeaway: Don't sleep on the Panthers offense. Carolina gave up 59 points to Chicago in Week 1, which overshadowed a solid offensive performance of their own. The Panthers scored 37 points and gained 478 yards of offense against the Bears. Of course, the defensive no-show made it all for naught. But after another 30+ point performance, suddenly it looks like Bryce Young's step forward in 2025 wasn't a fluke and he might be taking another step in 2026. ATLANTA FALCONS ARE DEALING WITH THE WORST QUARTERBACK SITUATION IN THE NFL AND IT ISN'T EVEN CLOSE Saints 24, Ravens 17 Takeaway: The Saints are a really fun team to watch. Last week, New Orleans nearly pulled off a massive upset of the Detroit Lions but fell just short. This week, they didn't let the opportunity slip away. More importantly, at least for general NFL fans, this team is fun. Tyler Shough, coming off a fan-voted Rookie of the Year season, doesn't look like a one-hit wonder. If Chris Olave can stay healthy, Saints-Panthers might be must-watch TV and that's not something I ever thought I'd type. Vikings 9, Bears 3 Takeaway: What a difference a week makes. A week ago, pundits were declaring that the 2026 Chicago Bears offense might be one of the greatest of all time. That was.. premature. Now, there's nothing more important than the health of quarterback Caleb Williams, who was carted off the field in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury. But Chicago didn't look great even when Williams was in the game. Weather was a factor, of course, but the two teams that scored 98 points combined in Week 1 only mustered 12 in Week 2. Bengals 20, Texans 6 Takeaway: If the Bengals can win games like this, the rest of the NFL is in trouble. In the Joe Burrow era, the Bengals have basically relied on their star quarterback to help them outscore opponents. This game was the opposite. In fact, Houston outgained Cincinnati by over 100 yards and had 10 more first downs. But the Bengals defense kept clamping down, forcing four turnovers on downs and only allowing two field goals. If Cincinnati's defense can almost singlehandedly win games, the Bengals are one of the best teams in the league. Patriots 20, Steelers 3 Takeaway: The Steelers are not a fun team to watch. Right now, Pittsburgh is like the anti-New Orleans. While the Saints have a young quarterback and a young receiver helping them move the ball up and down the field, the Steelers have an old quarterback whose career probably should have ended three years ago and an overpaid veteran receiver who can't catch anything. That's not a fun combination. Packers 20, Jets 17 Takeaway: I honestly don't know what to even think about this game. I was ready to declare that the Jets might actually be good, then they blew a 10-point fourth-quarter lead to the Packers and I'm back on the "oh wait, they're still the Jets" train. Similarly, what even are the Packers? They had a huge lead last week against the Vikings, blew it, and looked dead in the water for three quarters against the Jets. I guess they're just this year's ultimate Jekyll and Hyde team. They look fantastic at times and utterly terrible at others. Eagles 24, Titans 20 Takeaway: The Eagles' record is perfect, but their play is anything but. There are no moral victories in the NFL, so you'd much rather be 2-0 and playing bad than 0-2 with two heartbreaking losses despite great play. That said, I'm not sure how Eagles fans can feel great about this team right now. They barely scraped by the Commanders in Week 1 and then needed a last-second touchdown to avoid an upset against one of the worst teams in the NFL. The inconsistency that haunted the team last year is still present, and the Cowboys and Giants are both improved. The NFC East is no longer theirs to lose. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Browns 23, Buccaneers 19 Takeaway: The Bucs might just be bad. Losing to Cincinnati in Week 1 wasn't exactly shame-inducing, but a home loss to the Cleveland Browns is exactly that. Tampa's defense made Deshaun Watson look like a competent NFL quarterback for the first time in like 5 years and the offense really couldn't do much. They might have entered the season as NFC South favorites, but it's clear right now that both the Saints and Panthers are better teams. 49ers 35, Dolphins 13 Takeaway: The Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. This won't come as much of a surprise to anyone who follows the league, but yeah, the Dolphins are terrible. The good news is that they are tanking properly and an 0-17 season isn't out of the question. The two other teams that could have staked a claim as the league's worst, the Titans and Browns, both showed up in Week 2 (and the Browns even won). Not only did the Dolphins lose, but they were run out of the building. They might be a historically bad team by the time the season ends. Broncos 20, Jaguars 13 Takeaway: Sean Payton is still overrated. To be honest, I don't have much to say about this game. So, I decided to just remind everyone of my hottest NFL take. Sean Payton is a good NFL coach and he's treated like an elite one. He isn't, and the Broncos aren't that good. They'll be exposed in the next two weeks against the Rams and 49ers. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Raiders 26, Chargers 14 Takeaway: The Chargers' season is over. This might seem extreme, but I don't think it is. The Chargers have now lost games against the Cardinals and Raiders, not exactly world-beaters. Now, look at their upcoming schedule: at Buffalo, at Seattle, Denver, at Kansas City, at Los Angeles Rams, Houston, at Baltimore. It's possible the Chargers are going to be underdogs in each of their next seven games. I don't know how they recover at this point. Seahawks 31, Cardinals 7 Takeaway: The Seahawks defense is very much the league's best. There was a debate last year over whether it was the Seahawks or Broncos that featured the league's top unit but there's no such argument so far this year. Seattle held New England to 10 points in Week 1 and came up with a game-winning interception of Drake Maye. The Cardinals put up nearly 400 yards in Week 1 against the Chargers only to have the Seahawks hold them to 151 yards in Week 2. The NFC West is so stacked it almost seems unfair. Cowboys 37, Commanders 20 Takeaway: Injuries stink. I was excited to see Jayden Daniels bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 and return to his 2024 Rookie of the Year form. Then, right at the end of the first half, Daniels suffered another elbow injury and likely faces a lengthy absence. That stinks. For Dallas, it was a good response to the egg they laid in Week 1 against the Giants but the Daniels injury makes it hard to draw too many conclusions from this victory. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Chiefs 33, Colts 30 Takeaway: Is it possible for both teams to be happy? Yes, the Colts lost and are now 0-2. Yes, I wrote earlier that teams would much rather be 2-0 playing poorly than 0-2 and playing well. But after getting blown out of their own building in Week 1 by the Ravens, this was a major step forward. And the good news is the Colts face the Texans, Commanders, Steelers, Titans and Vikings in their next 5 games, and all five of those games are winnable. For the Chiefs, what is there to say? They look great and poised to make another run at a Super Bowl.

articles.title: NFL's dumbest moment of Week 2 goes to Jets coach Aaron Glenn who played not to lose at end of regulation
articles.summary: Sometimes the dumbest NFL play is a coaching decision. Aaron Glenn admitted he never considered a timeout that could have saved the Jets' game.
articles.body: Sometimes, the dumbest play of the week in the NFL is not actually a play at all but a play-call or decision by a coach. We're looking at you, Aaron Glenn. The New York Jets coach, in his second season with the Jets making all the decisions, has been a study in inconsistency with his clock management. And he was downright worthy of hard questioning on Sunday after a 20-17 overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers – because maybe this game didn't need to go to overtime at all. STEFON DIGGS GUILTY OF NFL'S DUMBEST MOVE OF WEEK 1 AND IT MAY HAVE DECIDED COMMANDERS LOSS TO EAGLES But Glenn curiously decided it would. In the fourth quarter, you see, the Packers had the ball and the Jets limited them to a 5-yard completion on third-and-10. So the Packers faced a fourth-down play with about 50 seconds left to play. Glenn could have immediately called time out. He could have immediately forced the Packers to punt on fourth down from midfield and given his offense one final opportunity in regulation to perhaps run three or four plays, get in field goal range, and pull out a win. Glenn had timeouts. But he didn't use them. He apparently didn't even think of using them. "I didn't," Glenn admitted after the game. "I didn't consider using that. I know exactly what you're talking about. No, I didn't think of using the timeout at that point at all." Fair enough. If we're giving Glenn the benefit of the doubt, we have to believe he probably thought it all through and made an informed decision. But informed decisions come with reasoning. So what was Glenn's reasoning for not using time-outs that would have given his offense a chance? "Man, I want to go back and really look at it, you know, to be honest with you," Glenn said. "I think they were in a situation where they were trying a no-brainer, and they took the no-brainer, or they took the penalty on that." The Packers did indeed praise Jesus that Glenn didn't call time out, so they did the no-brainer thing and sat on the ball and took a delay of game penalty. The 10-second runoff on the penalty left only two seconds on the clock. And the Packers, intent on launching a Hail Mary on fourth down, suffered a Jordan Love sack instead, to end regulation. But, again, if Glenn had called that timeout immediately after the third-down play, the Jets might have had maybe those 50 seconds to force Green Bay to punt and give their offense a chance. "Yeah, and if they would have punted it, that would put us in a backed-up situation," Glenn argued. "They could have punted the ball and put us in a backed-up situation right there. So that was the reason why." This is not the way. If Glenn had forced the issue, he actually has no clue what might have happened next. The punter might have dropped the snap. The punt might have gotten blocked. His punt returner, challenged as he's been with holding on to the ball, might have contributed a dynamic return. But instead, Glenn made certain his offense would have no final opportunity to win the game in regulation. New York Jets fans and the media covering the team, being the understanding and patient people they are, obviously excused Glenn's strategy. No, wait—no, they didn't. "This debacle falls on Aaron Glenn," the attention-grabbing part of a New York Post headline blared. Fans also took to social media and roasted Glenn. "Playing not to lose," one said. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "AG should not be a head coach IMHO," another offered. "Banking TO that can't ever be recovered," another said. "Even if they pin you, you still have the ball and a T.O. and a chance. Crazy." All of these are accurate and show how dumb Glenn's end-of-game decision actually was. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Eagles coach needs IV as 157 degree turf temps melt cleats, but Philly escapes with win at Titans
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni had only one thought with his offense on the field on a day so hot he needed intravenous fluids to cool off.
articles.body: Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni had only one thought with his offense on the field on a day so hot he needed intravenous fluids to cool off. Play to win. Jalen Hurts threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with nine seconds left, and the Eagles beat the Tennessee Titans 24-20 on a steamy Sunday when the temperature on the artificial turf was measured at 157 degrees Fahrenheit. “They fought and they clawed and they scratched and did anything they had to do to get the win,” Sirianni said of his Eagles. Philadelphia (2-0) appeared ready to dominate Tennessee. The Eagles opened the game by stringing together three straight drives of at least 11 plays. The Titans (0-2) sacked Hurts three times and picked him off twice, turning those into 10 points. Marcus Harris’ interception set up Joey Slye’s 33-yard field goal with 1:56 left, putting Tennessee up 20-17. Hurts had 1:56 to drive the Eagles 65 yards for the win. He finished with 264 yards passing and two TDs. Hurts called the drive the result of execution, focus and perseverance. “I’m not one to harp on the elements, but it was a challenge for us as a unit collectively,” Hurts said. “And I’m happy with how we weathered through that.” The TD catch was the first of Cooper’s career. DeVonta Smith had 10 catches for 117 yards, Tank Bigsby ran for a TD, and Jake Elliott kicked a 58-yard field goal. Cam Ward got the Titans to midfield, but his final pass under pressure hit the turf harmlessly as time expired. “It’s not a moral victory, it’s a loss,” Ward said. “That’s all it comes down to.” Philadelphia improved to 15-4 in September since 2021 and remained tied with Buffalo for the most wins in the NFL’s opening month in that span. The Eagles had plenty of fans in the stands, making it feel more like a home game. The air temperature reached 98 degrees Fahrenheit (37 Celsius) in the fourth quarter and felt like 106 degrees. It was so hot the Titans squirted water on players’ cleats on the sideline to cool them off. Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said he dismissed talk of the Titans’ cleats melting last week. “It’s like a very deceiving heat out there,” Mailata said. “It just sucks everything out of you.” The Titans hadn’t started a season with back-to-back home games since 2010. It didn’t help new coach Robert Saleh as Tennessee lost its first two for a third straight season. Saleh said he thought his Titans outplayed the Eagles at times. “They executed better in critical moments,” Saleh said. Ward threw for 183 yards and ran for a pair of 1-yard TDs. Three-time Pro Bowl running back Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger in his left arm on the opening play, though he returned to start the third quarter. He finished with 9 yards on four carries, his fourth career game held under 10 yards rushing. Philadelphia seemed ready to run the Titans off their own field, starting the game with a 15-play drive. But Hooker picked off Hurts’ pass to Smith in the end zone and set up Ward’s 1-yard TD run for the lead. The Eagles led 14-10 at halftime despite holding the ball for nearly 22 minutes. Slye pulled the Titans closer with a 37-yard field goal as the second quarter expired. Elite company for Sirianni and Hurts The Eagles are 2-0 for the fourth time under Sirianni, which is the most by a coach in franchise history. Sirianni became just the fourth NFL coach to win the first six road openers of a career, joining Sean McVay and George Allen (seven) and Mike McCarthy (six), according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Hurts trails Roger Staubach (eight) as the only NFL quarterbacks to start their careers winning at least their first six road openers. Hurts is the fifth quarterback in NFL history to win six straight road openers during any stretch of their career, joining Dan Fouts (nine), Staubach (eight), Bart Starr (seven) and Fran Tarkenton (seven).

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 2 Game vs. Buccaneers
articles.summary: Todd Monken had the Cleveland Browns looking like a functioning NFL franchise in a 23-19 Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Todd Monken had the Cleveland Browns looking like a functioning NFL franchise in a 23-19 Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

That was not a sentence most were expecting after a disastrous start to the season in Jacksonville.

In fact, it wasn't a sentence many were expecting at halftime. The Browns had just 59 yards of offense with 50 yards in penalties after the first two quarters.

Then the quarterback and the head coach turned things around to put together a strong second half and an upset victory.

That eases the tension heading into Week 3's home opener against the Carolina Panthers. Here's a quick assessment of how everyone looked before they get to play in front of the Dawg Pound next week.

Don't pencil in Shedeur Sanders as the starter just yet. Deshaun Watson staved off any talk of being benched before the home opener with his performance in the win.

Watson looked like a different quarterback in Week 2. One of the most notable developments was his play under pressure. was unable to handle pressure in Week 1, but actually thrived under it in multiple situations against the Buccaneers.

He converted a crucial 3rd-and-4 with his legs on the game-winning drive in the fourth quarter. He also delivered a few strikes with pressure in his face to move the chains.

He wasn't the most aggressive thrower. There were plenty of checkdowns that helped his 80 percent completion rate, but this was as good of a start as he's put together as a Cleveland Brown.

The statline for Judkins was even uglier in Week 2 than it was in Week 1. He only had 21 yards on his 12 carries and nine of them came on one run.

Still, he gets a slightly higher grade than last week because he did look more explosive. There wasn't much daylight for him and five of his carries were into an eight-man box .

Again, the run blocking was not great, but Sanders did more harm than good to the offense this week. He was at fault for Keionte Scott's getting to Watson unabated when he didn't pick up the blitz. He contributed just four yards on his two carries and seven on his lone reception.

Concepcion once again operated as the Browns primary underneath/screen target. They manufactured touches for the rookie and he caught all six of his targets.

The good news is that he cleaned up the ball security issues. He didn't lose a fumble this week, but he also didn't do much with his touches. He was contained for 28 yards on his six catches, but it's clear that Monken is looking to get him involved in the gameplan in multiple ways.

Last week, it could be argued that Denzel Boston's production was a case of too little, too late. Not so this week. Boston once again showed he's the Browns best big play threat with a 55-yard touchdown highlighting a five-catch, 95 yard day.

Boston proved to be difficult to bring down, breaking a tackle after catching the deep ball for a touchdown. He was given nearly a quarter of the team's targets and he held up his end of the bargain.

Jeudy was an afterthought in the offense for the second week in a row. The veteran had just one target and it was incomplete. That kind of production is a hard pill to swallow when he accounts for the third-largest cap hit on the team.

Fannin had some mistakes in the first half that kept this grade from being higher. He dropped a pass on third down (although it was short of the sticks anyway) and had an outside zone block that blew up the play.

But overall, this was a much better performance than Week 1. He kept the chains moving with five receptions for 54 yards.

Whiteheart made an appearance in the passing game for the second week in a row. He was mostly schemed open on his touchdow snag, but should get credit for getting it in the endzone.

The first-round pick drew a tough assignment in Week 1, but bounced back with a stronger performance in Week 2. Going from Josh Hines-Allen to Yaya Diaby and the Bucs front worked wonders for the rookie.

He wasn't charged with a single pressure in the pass game and looked much more NFL-ready. Unfortunately, it's hard to go much higher for any of the offensive line given the run game woes.

It's only two games, but Zion Johnson's Cleveland tenure is off to a rough start. He added another holding penalty to his ledger. He didn't outright give up any sacks, but he was part of the issue for a struggling run game that just couldn't get anything going.

The fact that Calijah Kancey and Vita Vea were held relatively quiet helps out the grade for all three interior blockers.

Raheim Sanders might have been to blame for Keionte Scott's running free on a blitz, but Watson might have come free if Jenkins won his rep. A'Shawn Robinson beat him across the face on the blitz, opening a bigger gap for Scott to run through and ultimately brought down Watson.

Add in the run-game woes, and it was another tough game for Jenkins.

Barber wasn't charged with any pressures by Next Gen Stats . That's another positive after a strong debut last week. Unfortunately, he did have a holding penalty that wiped out a decent Judkins run.

He played well enough to continue to start, but there are definitely things for him clean up going into Week 3.

Howard was a liability for much of this game. The only thing the Browns have been able to count on him for through two weeks is jumping offsides in critical situations. He had a false start on third down for the second time in two games.

Howard gave up another sack when he gave up a soft edge to David Walker. It's becoming more apparent why the Texans played him at guard.

We're still waiting for Jared Verse to make himself known as the team's top edge-rusher. Verse was once again held in check by the opposing offensive line. Going against Tristan Wirfs certainly doesn't help, but Verse only had one tackle on the day.

It was a TFL, so there are some positives, but he's not living up to expectations at this point.

McGuire made his presence felt at times on Sunday. He notched four tackles including one for a loss. The TFL set the tone on first down for a three-and-out in the second half that helped swing momentum to Cleveland.

Graham continues to be the engine that is running the defense. The Browns had issues stopping the run, but that wasn't on Graham. He was a disruptive force on the inside and it showed up in the box score.

He had three tackles, one for a loss, a sack and two quarterback hits. He also drew a holding call in the second quarter. He continues to look like he's going to have a massive sophomore campaign.

Collins is at his best when he's able to shoot gaps as a pass-rusher, but his weaknesses as a run defender are being exposed. It's easier to stomach that when he's doing things as a pass-rusher, but he was relatively quiet on that front this week.

Huntington is supposed to be a run-stuffing defensive tackle, but the Browns defense wasn't doing much run-stuffing. He got washed down on Bucky Irving's 38-yard run in the first half and only registered one tackle on the afternoon.

Schwesinger's statline is nearly identical to last week, but his grade is much higher. He looked much more like himself against the Bucs with the sideline-to-sideline range to make plays.

His takedown of Baker Mayfield on the Buccaneers' final drive was huge in making sure that the two-minute drill went the Browns' way.

Williams wasn't completely frozen in coverage this Sunday. That's a step in the right direction. The most encouraging thing from Williams is that most of his six tackles were close to the line of scrimmage. He played downhill and made tackles in the open field.

Ward was knocked over by Tyson Campbell on the touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka so it's hard to get too worked up over that. Still, it looked like Egbuka had the leverage before the trip.

Regardless, Ward didn't have any other major issues and the Buccaneers' passing game was largely held in check.

Campbell is playing through an ankle injury and he even left the game at one point Sunday. Unfortunately, he looks like a player who isn't at 100 percent right now. He ran into Ward on the touchdown to Egbuka and he was also the nearest defender when Tez Johnson hauled in a 49-yarder.

The Browns should take a serious look at whether Mekhi Blackmon can play if Campbell isn't fully healthy.

Last week, the Jaguars had a lot of success picking on Myles Harden. This week, Baker Mayfield paid for throwing it in his direction.

Harden did a good job to get his eyes on Mayfield and position himself under the comeback route to make a jumping interception. He was actually in position to make another pick in the red zone, but a collision with the receiver knocked the bal out.

Regardless, the slot did not look like a weakness this week.

Delpit was all over the field in a good way on Sunday. He was tied for the team lead with five solo tackles, registered a sack as a blitzer and was sticky in coverage throughout the game with no major faults.

Hickman had a nearly identical game to Delpit. He also recorded a sack as a blitzer and had another pressure where he was unable to bring down Mayfield. He was key in run support, making his tackles within the first five yards on a few runs.

The game was a field goal fest in the first half and Szmyt kept the Browns in it by going 3-for-3 with a long of 50.

No complaints for the punter here. Two of his four punts were downed inside the 20 and he averaged 49.5 yards on his four reps.

Sanders and Malachi Corley shared the kick return responsibilities this week. Sanders was unable to break one like he did in Week 1, but they didn't hurt the team either.

articles.title: NFL’s Azeez Al-Shaair pays tribute to slain Palestinian girl Wafaa Akila
articles.summary: Al-Shaair wears eye black with Akila’s name despite being fined for displaying messages about Israel’s genocide in Gaza.
articles.body:
American football player Azeez Al-Shaair has persisted with his stance on raising awareness about slain Palestinian children by wearing eye black bearing the name of Wafaa Akila, an eight-year-old girl killed by Israeli forces in Gaza, during his latest appearance in the National Football League (NFL).

The Houston Texans’ linebacker wore the black tape across his nose during a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, days after he wore the name of Hind Rajab on his eye black, which led to an $11,941 fine by the NFL as he breached the league’s code of conduct on players’ clothing and equipment during a match against the Buffalo Bills on September 13.

However, basketball player Kyrie Irving stepped in and offered to pay the fine for Al-Shaair, who later confirmed that he had been in touch with the nine-time NBA All-Star.

Al-Shaair brushed off talk of the fine while speaking to reporters last week. “It’s bigger to me; what’s a life worth? Is a life worth $11,000? No, I think it’s priceless,” he said.

In his first match appearance since being fined, Al-Shaair took the field with “Wafaa Akila” written on his eye black, a sticker or paint frequently used by NFL players to reduce glare.

On September 6, the first day of school for the eight-year-old, she was killed along with her father in an Israeli attack in western Gaza as they were making their way home.

The Israeli drone struck their car, leaving it burned and charred, with only a few pages of Akila’s school books surviving the horrific attack. A few hours earlier, a smiling Akila posed for a photo before setting off for her first day of school.

The Israeli genocide in Gaza has severely limited education for the Strip’s 660,000 children, with 90 percent of schools left damaged or destroyed.

Israel has killed at least 21,500 children since October 7, 2023, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza .

Akila’s death was similar to that of Rajab, aged five, who was killed in Gaza after Israeli soldiers opened fire on her family’s stranded car on January 29, 2024. A phone call by the Palestine Red Crescent Society documented her final moments and was the subject of an Oscar-nominated docudrama.

Al-Shaair shared posts about Akila, as well as her mother’s reaction to the killing, on his Instagram account on Sunday.

Following the Texans’ match against the Bengals, a social media user posted a video that showed Al-Shaair interacting with children – some sporting keffiyehs, others who were amputees and were holding posters in support of the player – on the sidelines.

Al-Shaair, a Black American Muslim player, has frequently spoken about the plight of Palestinians and has paid the price for it .

He was also fined in January, during the NFL’s last season, for displaying the message “Stop The Genocide” on his nose tape. While it did not specifically refer to a particular conflict, it was widely understood to be about Gaza and Sudan.

Prominent American Muslim scholar Omar Suleiman has repeatedly voiced his support for Al-Shaair.

“My brother, who went to Jordan to be with Palestinian refugees this summer, who spends time with Palestinian children with missing limbs in Houston, who is using every week of his Pro Bowl NFL career to honour a Palestinian child despite the fines,” Suleiman wrote about Al-Shaair in a social media post on Sunday.

“In the sports and entertainment arenas run by many of the same types of people who run government, choose to be like Azeez Al-Shaair, Kyrie, and Macklemore.”

The NFL’s fine on Al-Shaair comes at a time when Robert Kraft , owner of the Boston-based team New England Patriots, confirmed that he pressured pop star Ed Sheeran to drop rapper Macklemore from his tour of the United States.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Chiefs Make NFL History in OT Win vs. Daniel Jones, Colts
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce combined to pull off something that has never been done before in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce combined to pull off something that has never been done before in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Mahomes continues to shine in prime time and he now has the longest winning streak for a QB in overtime contests.

Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, while Kelce caught nine passes for 101 yards and one score. According to Opta , this was the first time a team had a quarterback 30 or older eclipse 300 yards and a tight end 35 or older go for 100 yards receiving.

Kelce's stat line was notable in another regard:

"I'm grateful I'm on this team right now," the 11-time Pro Bowler told ESPN's Scott Van Pelt (4:05 mark). "This team, we go out and we play hard for each other every single play. There was never a doubt we were gonna find a way to get a win tonight."

Mahomes' performance was a strong statement to those who wondered what kind of quarterback he'd be after making a relatively quick recovery from a torn ACL.

The season is only two games old. Teams that start well can fall off and those that start poorly can turn things around.

But Kansas City's 2-0 record looks like a warning sign to the AFC and the rest of the league. With Mahomes healthy, the Chiefs are back among the contenders.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Reacts to Browns Win, Monken's 'F--k That' Quote in Video amid Shedeur Sanders Rumors
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said he's "right where I'm supposed to be" following Sunday's 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said he's "right where I'm supposed to be" following Sunday's 23-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

"Leave the journey in God's hands, keep working hard, keep pushing forward and let the outcome be the outcome when it comes," he told reporters .

The three-time Pro Bowler went 24-of-30 for 238 yards and two touchdowns in the victory. In what was reportedly an important week for sorting out the quarterback room, Watson made a strong case for himself with Shedeur Sanders waiting in the wings.

Overcoming a 10-point deficit in the second half and knocking off the Bucs on the road raised the collective spirits inside the locker room. Coach Todd Monken referenced the general narrative around the organization and said his players were motivated to silence the skeptics.

"'Browns are gonna Browns.' F--k that," Monken said after the win. "The guys took that to heart."

Watson's account differed a bit, but he agreed with the overall sentiment.

"I wouldn't say it was a topic of conversation," he said (2:01 mark). "I just think that Monk said what he said. That's how we all feel."

Nothing gets a disgruntled fanbase back on board like winning games. The positivity in Cleveland could be fleeting, though.

One win is unlikely to have canceled out all of the frustration and angst toward Watson. Should his performance go backward in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, the critics will be back out in full force, and people will wonder once again whether it's time to hand the keys to the offense over to Sanders.

articles.title: Colts Actually Wanted to Go For It on 4th-and-8 in OT, Everything Steichen Said After Chiefs Loss
articles.summary: Before attempting a game-tying field goal in overtime against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen considered going for a game-winning touchdown.
articles.body:
Before attempting a game-tying field goal in overtime against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football , Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen considered going for a game-winning touchdown.

While facing a fourth-and-8, the Colts conservatively opted to kick a field goal that tied the game, but the Chiefs still had enough time in the extra period to set up a 40-yard field goal by Harrison Butker as time expired to secure a 33-30 win.

Per ESPN's Stephen Holder , Steichen said after the game that he was prepared to go for it on fourth down if the Chiefs showed favorable coverage against the Colts' play call.

"We wanted it to be the last possession," Steichen said. After calling a timeout, he said he told quarterback Daniel Jones, "If you love it, man, let's go at it. Let's go win this thing. But if it's not the right look … let's kick the field goal here."

The Chiefs showed a coverage that forced Steichen's hand, as the Colts accepted a delay-of-game penalty and settled for a field goal. Kansas City's game-winning drive sent Indianapolis to 0-2 to start the season for the second time in the last three years.

Steichen also defended his decision to defer after the Colts won the overtime coin toss, saying he felt his team would have the advantage in knowing what was needed after the Chiefs' first possession.

"If we go first … [Patrick] Mahomes gets four downs going the other way," Steichen said. "It could go either way in those situations."

The Colts will try to bounce back in Week 3 when they face the AFC South rival Houston Texans, who will also be seeking their first win of the season.

articles.body: Travis Kelce reminded the NFL why he remains one of the Kansas City Chiefs' most trusted weapons. After a quiet start to the 2026 season, the veteran tight end delivered a standout performance against the Indianapolis Colts on September 20. His nine catches, 101 receiving yards and touchdown helped Kansas City secure a thrilling 33-30 overtime win, giving Kelce and Patrick Mahomes another memorable night together.Travis Kelce's 2026 stats show a strong start after Week 2Kelce opened the season against the Denver Broncos on September 14, recording three receptions for 71 yards. Although he did not score a touchdown, his 59-yard catch showed he could still make big plays downfield.The Colts game brought a much bigger impact. Kelce caught nine of his 11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown, giving Kansas City a reliable option throughout the contest. His longest reception was 18 yards, and he found the end zone for the first time this season.Through two games, Kelce has recorded 12 receptions for 172 yards and one touchdown. His average stands at 14.3 yards per catch, a notable increase from his 11.2-yard average in 2025.The performance also came at a key moment for the Chiefs. Kansas City needed every contribution in a game that went to overtime, and Kelce's ability to turn targets into consistent gains helped keep the offense moving.Travis Kelce's career stats highlight years of consistencyKelce's latest performance adds to a career built on steady production. The Chiefs tight end has remained a central part of the offense across multiple seasons, delivering strong receiving numbers even as the team has changed around him.His 2022 campaign stands out as one of his most productive. Kelce finished that season with 110 receptions, 1,338 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. In 2020, he recorded 105 catches for 1,416 yards and 11 touchdowns, showcasing his ability to stretch the field and make plays in the red zone.He continued to produce in the following years. Kelce posted 93 receptions for 984 yards in 2023, followed by 97 catches for 823 yards in 2024. In 2025, he finished with 76 receptions, 851 yards and five touchdowns across 17 regular-season games.Now in his 14th NFL season, Kelce is adding to an impressive body of work.
